habitat: Singly on the shores of rivers, lakes, dams, estuaries and rocky coasts. It bobs its hindquarters and flies low with stiff, downward-bowed wings.
summary: A common summer visitor, with a few present all year. The upperparts and breast-band are dark brown, and the white underparts extend around the folded wing. The upper tail is white barred brown. Flushed birds give a shrill twee-wee-wee. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Common Sandpiper and the code NB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: Medium-short and robust. The colour is not given.

head.pattern: The identification line does not separate the head from the dark brown upperparts.

upperparts.pattern: Upperparts dark brown. In flight there is no white rump, a faint wing-bar, and white outer tail feathers.

underparts.pattern: Dark brown breast-band. White below extends around the folded wing.

wings.pattern: A faint wing-bar in flight. White shows above the folded wing.

tail.shape: White upper tail barred brown, with white outer feathers in flight.

viewNotes.note: Dark brown above, with white extending around the folded wing and a dark brown breast-band.
Dark brown breast-band and white below.
Dark brown upperparts. The upper tail is white barred brown.
No white rump, a faint wing-bar, and white outer tail feathers. The wings beat with a flicking action below the horizontal.
The underwing colour is not given.
Flies low with stiff, downward-bowed wings.

calls.description: When flushed it utters a shrill 'twee-wee-wee'. No grade A recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A flight call from Poland. The filename is XC187104-Actitis_hypoleucos_Poland_Jarek_Matusiak_20140713_28.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer visitor, with a few present all year, and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. Avibase does not mark it rare. No grade A recording from South Africa was found; a grade B recording from South Africa exists. The leg colour is not given. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^11=2048 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 1024–4096.
